[GitHub Repository](https://github.com/shuyang9527/BIOSTAT721-Project2)

This report summarizes daily carbon monoxide (CO), fine particulate matter
(PM2.5), and ozone (O3) measurements from the EPA monitor at Raleigh-Durham
International Airport (RDU). The data cover 2018 and 2019, and January through
April of 2020.

```{r prepare-data, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)

# Load the cleaning function and read all three files using ppm for ozone.
source("clean_air_quality.R")

aq_2018 <- clean_air_quality("data/AQ_2018.csv")
aq_2019 <- clean_air_quality("data/AQ_2019.csv")
aq_2020 <- clean_air_quality("data/AQ_2020.csv")

air_quality <- rbind(aq_2018, aq_2019, aq_2020)

# Confirm expected row counts, unique dates, and nonnegative concentrations.
stopifnot(
  nrow(aq_2018) == 361L,
  nrow(aq_2019) == 365L,
  nrow(aq_2020) == 121L,
  !anyNA(air_quality$date),
  anyDuplicated(air_quality$date) == 0L,
  !any(air_quality[c("co", "pm25", "o3")] < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
)

# Create common month and year labels for the summaries and plots.
air_quality$year <- format(air_quality$date, "%Y")
air_quality$month <- factor(
  format(air_quality$date, "%m"),
  levels = sprintf("%02d", 1:12),
  labels = month.abb
)
```

## Annual Minimum and Maximum Daily Concentrations

```{r annual-tables, results='asis'}
pollutant_labels <- c(
  co = "Carbon monoxide (ppm)",
  pm25 = "Fine particulate matter (µg/m³ LC)",
  o3 = "Ozone (ppm)"
)

# Summarize the observed daily concentrations separately for each year.
for (year in c("2018", "2019", "2020")) {
  year_data <- air_quality[air_quality$year == year, ]
  measurements <- year_data[names(pollutant_labels)]

  annual_range <- data.frame(
    Pollutant = unname(pollutant_labels),
    Minimum = vapply(measurements, min, numeric(1), na.rm = TRUE),
    Maximum = vapply(measurements, max, numeric(1), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

  period <- if (year == "2020") "January–April 2020" else year

  print(knitr::kable(
    annual_range,
    digits = 3,
    format.args = list(nsmall = 3),
    row.names = FALSE,
    caption = paste(
      "Minimum and maximum daily pollutant concentrations at RDU:",
      period
    )
  ))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Monthly Carbon Monoxide and Ozone Concentrations

```{r monthly-co-ozone, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Monthly mean CO and ozone concentrations at RDU with 95% confidence intervals."}
# Pool available daily readings by calendar month across years.
monthly_co_o3 <- air_quality |>
  dplyr::select(month, co, o3) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(co, o3),
    names_to = "pollutant",
    values_to = "concentration"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(concentration)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(pollutant, month) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    average = mean(concentration),
    se = sd(concentration) / sqrt(n),
    lower = average - 1.96 * se,
    upper = average + 1.96 * se,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pollutant = factor(
      pollutant,
      levels = c("co", "o3"),
      labels = c("Carbon monoxide", "Ozone")
    )
  )

ggplot2::ggplot(
  monthly_co_o3,
  ggplot2::aes(x = month, y = average, color = pollutant)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbar(
    ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    width = 0.18
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ pollutant, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Carbon monoxide" = "#0072B2",
    "Ozone" = "#D55E00"
  )) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean concentration (ppm)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")
```

The panels use separate vertical scales so that month-to-month changes in both
pollutants are visible. January through April pool daily measurements from
three years; May through December pool measurements from two.

## Monthly PM2.5 Distributions by Year

```{r monthly-pm25, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Daily PM2.5 concentrations by month and year at RDU. The 2020 data cover January through April only."}
# Group the daily PM2.5 readings by calendar month and year.
pm25_data <- air_quality |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(pm25)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(year = factor(year))

ggplot2::ggplot(
  pm25_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = month, y = pm25, fill = year)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.75,
    outlier.size = 1,
    outlier.alpha = 0.55
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "2018" = "#0072B2",
    "2019" = "#E69F00",
    "2020" = "#009E73"
  )) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Month",
    y = "Daily PM2.5 concentration (µg/m³ LC)",
    fill = "Year"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )
```

Grouped boxplots show how the median and spread of daily PM2.5 concentrations
vary across years within each month.

## Interpretation

Mean CO concentrations were highest in late fall and early winter, while mean ozone concentrations were highest in June. The highest observed daily PM2.5
concentration was 31.200 µg/m³ LC in February 2020, even though that month had a lower median than February of the previous two years. Since the 2020 data end in April, they cannot support a full-year comparison with 2018 and 2019.

## AI Use Statement

I used ChatGPT to help draft the R code for cleaning, summarizing, and plotting the data. I ran the code myself in RStudio and checked the results, including cleaned row counts, date uniqueness, and the tables and figures in the Word document.
